chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Thal'abah ibn Maymoun, from Badr ibn al-Khalil al-Azdi, who said:

I was sitting in the presence of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), so he said: 'Two signs will occur before the rising of Al-Qaim (peace be upon him) which have not occurred since Adam descended to the earth: the sun will be eclipsed in the middle of the month of Ramadan, and the moon at its end.' A man said, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah! The sun is eclipsed at the end of the month, and the moon in the middle.' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'I know what you say, but these two signs have not occurred since Adam (peace be upon him) descended.'

key_terms.قِيَامِ الْقَائِمِ: The rising/standing of the Awaited Imam

ai.seo_question: What are the two unique celestial signs before the rise of Al-Qaim?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) identifies a rare celestial phenomenon—a solar eclipse in the middle of Ramadan and a lunar eclipse at its end—as unique signs preceding the rise of Al-Qaim (peace be upon him). These events, which have not occurred since Adam’s descent to earth, serve as distinct eschatological markers in Shia tradition, emphasizing the cosmic scale of the Mahdi's emergence and the restoration of divine order.
